title: Giving Up a Granite Ridge Season Pass: Window, Grounds and What Comes Back
content:
A guest may give up a pass, and what comes back to them depends on when they say so and on how much of the season they have already taken.

**The window.** The cancellation is honoured for a refund only when it is recorded no later than the cancellation window counted in calendar days from the day the pass application was recorded. Calendar days are counted forward from the anchor date, the anchor date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; where the resulting boundary falls on a date that does not exist in the target month, the last day of that month is used. The comparison is not-later-than and the boundary day itself satisfies it.

**Inside the window.** The clause reading "Inside the window the refundable amount is worked out on the tier's refund basis: on the day use basis it is the price committed to, less the tier's cancellation fee, less the tier's day use deduction for each day already scanned on the pass; on the pro rata basis it is the price committed to, less the tier's cancellation fee, multiplied by the share of the season's operating days still to come" is **no longer in force**, and so is the clause reading "The refundable amount is never below zero". Both have been superseded: what the collective retains when a pass is given up, and what is issued back to the household, are governed by the current bases for those two figures. The cancellation window, the cancellation fee, the refund basis and the day use deduction published for each tier in this charter are unaffected and remain in force as the tier's published figures.

**Outside the window.** Outside the window nothing is refundable and the pass runs to the end of the season unless the guest still wants it cancelled for their own reasons.

**Medical grounds.** A cancellation given on medical grounds is honoured only when the collective's protection records already show a settled claim on a protection plan held by the same household account. The protection record answers this, not the guest's account of the injury or the note they hold.

**Not twice.** A pass record that already stands in the cancelled or closed state is not cancelled again.

**The form value comes back in.** What comes back is issued as resort credit against the pass record, and a return to the original payment method is a finance team decision rather than a desk decision.

### The window at its boundary

Hypothetical dates on a Granite Ridge Summit Pass, whose window is 21 calendar days: the application was recorded on the 1st of a month. Counting that day as day zero, day 21 falls on the 22nd.

| Day the cancellation is recorded | Calendar days since the application | Honoured for a refund |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the 22nd | 21 | yes, the boundary day satisfies it |
| the 23rd | 22 | no |

superseded_clauses: Inside the window the refundable amount is worked out on the tier's refund basis: on the day use basis it is the price committed to, less the tier's cancellation fee, less the tier's day use deduction for each day already scanned on the pass; on the pro rata basis it is the price committed to, less the tier's cancellation fee, multiplied by the share of the season's operating days still to come.
The refundable amount is never below zero.
